/** What an omitted token becomes, read back from the real derivation with every other token
 *  standing in as `var(<name>)`, so the table cannot drift from what Orca applies. */
function omittedValueFor(token: PluginAppThemeToken, base: 'light' | 'dark'): string {
  const others = Object.fromEntries(
    PLUGIN_APP_THEME_TOKENS.filter((other) => other !== token).map((other) => [
      other,
      `var(${other})`
    ])
  )
  const cssFallback = pluginAppThemeCssFallback(token, base)
  if (cssFallback && 'tint' in cssFallback) {
    return `\`${cssFallback.tint}\` at ${cssFallback.percent}% opacity`
  }
  const derived = cssFallback
    ? 'mixForeground' in cssFallback
      ? `color-mix(in srgb, var(--foreground) ${cssFallback.mixForeground}%, var(${cssFallback.into ?? '--background'}))`
      : `var(${cssFallback[0]})`
    : completePluginAppThemeTokens(others)[token]
  if (derived === undefined) {
    return MODE_MIXES[token] ?? "Orca's built-in color"
  }
  const mix = /^color-mix\(in srgb, var\((--[\w-]+)\) (\d+)%, var\((--[\w-]+)\)\)$/.exec(derived)
  if (mix) {
    return `\`${mix[1]}\` mixed ${mix[2]}% into \`${mix[3]}\``
  }
  return derived.replace(/^var\((--[\w-]+)\)$/, 'same as `$1`')
}

function omittedValue(token: PluginAppThemeToken): string {
  const light = omittedValueFor(token, 'light')
  const dark = omittedValueFor(token, 'dark')
  return light === dark ? light : `light: ${light}; dark: ${dark}`
}

}

  Dark theme separately, and Orca paints the one for its current mode (following the OS under
  System). Contribute one theme of each base to ship a pair; installing it fills both slots.
- `--background` and `--foreground` are required. Every other public token is optional; an
  omitted token is derived from the ones you set (cards from `--background`, sidebars lifted a
  step off `--background` so the left sidebar keeps a visible edge, text from `--foreground`,
  sidebar accents from `--accent`, rings from `--primary`, and so on), so a two-token theme still
  colors the whole app.
- [Theme tokens](plugin-theme-tokens.md) lists every public token and what it falls back to
  when omitted. Other variables cannot be set.
- Values must be colors: hex, a color function (`rgb`, `hsl`, `oklch`, …) or a color name.
  `transparent`, `currentColor`, CSS-wide keywords, lengths, `calc()`, `var()` and `url()` are
  refused.

  `--primary`/`--primary-foreground`) must be opaque with at least 4.5:1 contrast; a pair that

# Expose agent and workspace status colors as plugin theme tokens

Closes #36697.

## Why

Plugin app themes should be able to recolor the agent and workspace status hues. Today a monochrome theme still shows Orca's yellow working dots and orange waiting dots on every workspace card. They are the loudest color in the sidebar, and no public token reaches them.

## What changes for theme authors

These eight tokens are now public, so a theme may set them in `tokens`:

- `--agent-working`, `--agent-question`, `--agent-question-text`
- `--workspace-status-done`, `--workspace-status-review`, `--workspace-status-progress`
- `--status-success`, `--status-warning`

An omitted token keeps Orca's built-in color, exactly as before. The `-background`, `-border` and `-text` tints of `--status-success` and `--status-warning` already derive from them with `color-mix`, so they follow the theme's value with no extra tokens.

Each new token goes through the existing renderer check, which drops only the failing token and keeps the shared surface:

| Token | Checked against | Minimum |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--agent-working`, `--agent-question`, `--workspace-status-*` | `--worktree-sidebar` | 1.5:1 |
| `--status-success`, `--status-warning` | `--background` | 1.5:1 |
| `--agent-question-text` | `--background` | 3:1 |

Values must also be opaque, like every other checked token.

## Why 1.5:1 for the hues

The 3:1 floor used for `--git-decoration-*` would refuse Orca's own defaults. Orca's light working yellow is about 1.8:1 on the light workspace sidebar, and its light done and progress hues are about 2.1:1. A theme that copied Orca's light palette would lose them. These hues mark state next to a label, so the check only has to keep them from vanishing. That matches the reasoning behind the ring check. `--agent-question-text` is legible text, so it keeps the 3:1 status-text floor, which Orca's own values clear in both modes (about 5.2:1 light and 11.6:1 dark).

The ratios above come from the sRGB equivalents of Tailwind v4's oklch colors. Treat them as approximate.

## Known limit

Native chat re-declares `--status-success` and `--status-warning` per chat scheme, as it already does for `--git-decoration-*` and the diff tokens. Inside chat, those two keep Orca's colors. The themes page now says so. Making chat follow the theme is a separate change.

## Compatibility

The public token list is additive. Older Orca clients skip unknown tokens in tolerant parsing, so a theme that sets these still loads there and simply keeps the built-in hues. `pnpm validate:plugin` on an older CLI would refuse them, as with any newly added token.

## Changes

- `plugin-theme-artifact.ts` adds the tokens to `PLUGIN_APP_THEME_TOKENS`.
- `plugin-theme-token-reference-doc.ts` says what each token paints. The `Record` keyed by token makes that required.
- `plugin-theme-tokens.ts` adds the contrast rules from one token-to-surface table.
- `docs/reference/plugin-theme-tokens.md` is regenerated from source, and `docs/reference/plugin-themes.md` documents the checks and fallback.
- `document-theme.test.ts` covers a theme with visible and vanishing status hues.

content.text:
The goal was to let a plugin theme recolor the agent and workspace status hues, so a monochrome theme no longer shows yellow and orange dots on every working or waiting workspace card. That's done. The eight tokens from the issue are now public theme tokens, and omitting one keeps today's color. Nothing is committed or pushed. The PR description is in `PR.md`.

**What changes for theme authors.** A theme can now set `--agent-working`, `--agent-question`, `--agent-question-text`, `--workspace-status-done/review/progress`, `--status-success` and `--status-warning`. The success and warning background, border and text tints already mix from the base colors, so they follow the theme's value. Older Orca clients skip unknown tokens, so such a theme still loads there with the built-in colors.

**Contrast checks.** Each new token goes through the existing renderer check, which drops only the failing token and never the surface it sits on.
- The five agent and workspace hues need 1.5:1 against `--worktree-sidebar`.
- `--status-success` and `--status-warning` need 1.5:1 against `--background`.
- `--agent-question-text` is text, so it gets the existing 3:1 status-text floor against `--background`.

**Decision for you: the 1.5:1 floor.** I didn't reuse the 3:1 floor that `--git-decoration-*` uses, because it would reject Orca's own defaults. I estimate the light working yellow at about 1.8:1 on the light sidebar, and the light done and progress hues at about 2.1:1. Those numbers come from Tailwind v4 sRGB equivalents I recalled, because Tailwind isn't vendored here, so treat them as approximate. These hues sit next to a label, so the check only needs to keep them visible. If you want a stricter floor, I can raise it, but a theme that copies Orca's light palette would then lose those hues.

**Known limit.** Inside native chat, `--status-success` and `--status-warning` stay at Orca's colors, because chat re-declares them for its light or dark scheme. It already does the same for the git-decoration and diff tokens. The sidebar dots from the issue aren't affected. The themes page now says this, and making chat follow the theme would be a separate change.

**Files changed.**
- `src/shared/plugins/artifacts/plugin-theme-artifact.ts` adds the tokens to the public list.
- `src/shared/plugins/artifacts/plugin-theme-token-reference-doc.ts` says what each token paints, and the type system requires an entry for every token.
- `src/renderer/src/lib/plugin-theme-tokens.ts` adds the contrast rules from one table mapping each token to its surface.
- `docs/reference/plugin-theme-tokens.md` is regenerated, and `docs/reference/plugin-themes.md` describes the checks and the fallback.
- `src/renderer/src/lib/document-theme.test.ts` has a new test: a theme with visible and vanishing status hues.

**Verification.**
- `document-theme.test.ts` and `plugin-theme-artifact.test.ts` pass (41 tests). The new test fails when the contrast rules are removed.
- I regenerated the token reference doc by calling `renderPluginThemeTokenReference()`, and its diff is exactly the eight new rows.
- `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` pass on the changed files.
- `tsc` on the web project reports nothing in the files I changed. Its other errors are all missing modules (`react`, `vitest`, `sonner`) or knock-on errors in files I didn't touch. I'm inferring they come from the environment and didn't run a baseline to confirm.

**Not run as the repo intends.** Several `node_modules` links here (`zod`, `yaml`, `ajv`) are broken, and the workspace packages are unbuilt. So `pnpm test` and `pnpm generate:plugin-schemas` couldn't run as-is, and I ran the tests under a minimal vitest config outside the repo instead. I also didn't launch the Electron app to look at the sidebar dots under a theme. CI should rerun the full checks.
